Reviews Are Not the Whole Story

Reviews matter for Google Maps ranking, but they are not the whole story. Volume alone does not decide who makes it to the top of the map pack.

That is good news if you do not have thousands of reviews yet. A well-built website, regular Google Business Profile posts, and a steady stream of detailed reviews with photos all help you win more of the map and more organic leads. This is the groundwork we put in for every client.

Channel 2 · Local Services Ads

Local Services Ads Are the Closest Thing to
Predictable HVAC Demand in Waco

If you already run Local Services Ads, look at your lead history before judging the channel.

Local Services Ads are one of the few advertising channels where you only pay when a qualified homeowner contacts you. You are not paying for clicks, impressions, or people who never pick up the phone. You are paying for direct opportunities from homeowners actively looking for HVAC help.

The problem is not that Local Services Ads do not work.

The problem is that most contractors never get past the feast-or-famine stage.

Illustrative economics for a well-run account. Your close rate, lead cost, and return will vary.

Why Most Waco Shops Get Feast or Famine From Local Services Ads

Google made Local Services Ads easy to start. But easy to start does not mean easy to scale.

Many HVAC companies experience the same pattern. A slow month brings four or five leads. Then a busy season arrives, demand increases, and the contractors who have built a strong Local Services Ads foundation are positioned to capture far more of that demand.

A well-managed Local Services Ads account can generate 15–60 qualified leads in a peak cooling month like July, depending on budget, market competition, reviews, services offered, and account setup.

The difference between four leads and dozens of opportunities usually comes down to the signals Google uses to decide who gets shown.

The goal is not simply turning Local Services Ads on.

The goal is building the foundation that lets the channel produce consistently when homeowners need you most.

Channel 2 · Pay-Per-Click

Pay-Per-Click Is What Separates the Shops
That Scale From the Ones That Stall

Local Services Ads get your phone ringing. Pay-per-click is what decides whether a Waco HVAC company climbs into seven and eight figures or stalls year after year.

It is no coincidence that every residential HVAC company in the greater Waco region that has scaled past $5 million in revenue runs Google Pay-Per-Click Ads.

Pay-per-click is not the sure thing Local Services Ads are. Campaigns need daily maintenance, careful keyword research, and dedicated landing pages with an offer worth clicking. More than half of Waco HVAC contractors do not run Google PPC at all, and some tried it, got poor results, and quit. Almost every time, that poor result traces back to a badly managed campaign, not to PPC itself.

Waco “AC repair” cost per click about $38, live Google Ads data, July 2026. Returns are illustrative of a well-run and a badly-run account.

Sarah’s Take

This Is Not a Lead Problem. It Is a System Problem.

Waco has no shortage of quality HVAC contractors doing outstanding work for their customers. That is the hardest thing to build, and it is the genuine quality that even the best marketing can never fake. If that describes your shop, you are already past the part most companies never get right.

What almost every contractor is missing is a system that keeps up with a market changing at lightning speed: ChatGPT answering homeowners directly, private equity buying up local shops, and AI that lets a small team build its own tools.

This is an exciting moment, and the winners will not be the biggest or best-funded companies. They will be the nimble operators who move fast, keep learning, and surround themselves with technicians, office staff, and marketers who share their vision. That is who we build these systems for.
One System. Every Channel Working Together.

Just Like HVAC Systems, Marketing Works Best When Every Component Works Together

Most HVAC contractors treat marketing like separate buckets. They hire one company for ads, another for SEO, and someone else to manage their Google Business Profile. The problem? None of those pieces are working together.

At RS Gonzales, we are digital marketing specialists for HVAC businesses. We build your marketing as one connected system, because the same things that help you rank in Google Maps also help your ads perform better and increase your chances of being recommended by AI.

Reviews

The contractors who win their markets are not the ones doing one thing well. They are the ones building a system where every channel strengthens the next. Method & Sources

How These Numbers Were Put Together

Method

Market sizing: U.S. Census owner-occupied housing for the Waco metro times industry-average annual HVAC spend per home. Search volume: Google Keyword Planner. Reviews and ratings: Google Business Profiles, July 2026. AI testing: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity. Keyword competition: live results-page analysis. Advertiser activity: live Google Local Services unit and Google Ads Transparency Center.

Market-size figures are directional estimates; treat every number as a July 2026 snapshot. Industry percentages are third-party figures, not RS Gonzales client results. Photographs are illustrative and do not depict any company named here. The kitchen illustration on this page is AI-generated; every other image is a real photograph or a real screen capture.

Sources

  1. WebFX 2026 — map pack about 44% of clicks, about 98% of local pages, 55.8% above organic with Local Services Ads.
  2. SparkToro / Datos 2026 — about 68% zero-click.
  3. Places Scout / PPC.land 2026 — map-pack ads under 3% to about 22%, November 2025 to January 2026.
  4. ALM Corp 2026 — paid click share doubled, organic down 23%, text ads 9% to 16%.
  5. Waco “AC repair” cost per click about $38, live Google Ads data, July 2026.
